findings.claim: Landscape terrain themes are NOT referenced by a global def-index stored in the chunk. They resolve via a THREE-level indirection: (1) per-cell byte = LOCAL palette slot, (2) per-map CMap palette at this+0x1a6c maps slot -> a GLOBAL theme def-index, (3) BuildThemes resolves that global index against the shared ENGINE_THEME table. So the chunk's per-cell bytes are only meaningful relative to the per-map palette that must be seeded correctly at map-open.
findings.engineEvidence: CMap::GetEngineThemeAt @008xxxxx (decomp line 3019-3041): reads a *byte* from per-cell data (*(byte*)(mapdata + cellIndex*0xc + 4 + param3)) and uses it as index*8 into the palette pointer at this+0x1a6c: return *(ulong*)(*(int*)(this+0x1a6c) + slot*8). CMap_InitializePalette @008f71a0 (line 697-728) zero-fills the 0x800-byte palette then seeds slot0 via AddThemeDefIndexToPalette(this, *(ulong*)(*(int*)(*(int*)(this+0x1c)+0xd0)+0x50)). AddThemeDefIndexToPalette @008f70f0 (line 742-788) stores a theme *def index* (param_1) into palette entry: *(ulong*)(this+0x1a6c + slot*8)=param_1.
findings.discrepancy: The baked ForgeTest chunk is a byte-clone of donor Darkwood9_Leadout_01, so its per-cell palette-slot bytes are valid, but they are only correct if the per-map palette is seeded from the SAME theme table/order the donor was baked against. Nothing in the STB chunk or CStaticMapInfoBlock carries the theme name table (lev.cpp:96-118 shows the 256-entry ground-theme NAME table lives in the .LEV, not the STB). The engine seeds the palette from live global CDefinitionManager state, not from the chunk.
findings.toolingEvidence: lev.cpp:96-106 (256 ground themes = 128-byte NAME + u32) and :162-181 (themeIndexAt reads cell[10+i] as a LOCAL index into that name table). stb_infoblock_baker.py:51-73 FIELDS list — CStaticMapInfoBlock has NO theme field at all, confirming the STB header cannot register themes.

findings.claim: BuildThemes populates a GLOBAL, shared, name-agnostic ENGINE_THEME vector strictly by index count. It takes no map name and is region-independent, so it cannot be fixed by any per-map name change. If the donor's theme indices are out of range for the resident ENGINE_THEME table at ForgeTest-open time, this is a name-agnostic co-cause.
findings.engineEvidence: CEngineLandscapeRenderer::BuildThemes @00b687d0 (line 485-683): GetIDFromSymbol('ENGINE_THEME') -> resize(this+0x4b8 vector, count) (line 512-527); loop calls CDefinitionManager::GetDef<CSoundThemeDef>(DAT_01436e28,'ENGINE_THEME',idx,...) (line 534) then indexes global DAT_01436e98+0x954 texture-bank array by uVar4 with a bounds check '(uVar4 < (count))' that falls back to iVar5=0 (line 557-566) — an out-of-range/zero index yields a null bank pointer, i.e. missing texture => white. GetDef<CSoundThemeDef> @ line 2104-2145 resolves purely by GetPDefFromGlobalIndex(param_2) — GLOBAL index, no name.
findings.discrepancy: BuildThemes writes into a shared global vector (this+0x4b8) and reads the shared global DAT_01436e98 def-manager; a bad index for ForgeTest corrupts/whitens the shared table, matching the observed tell that teleporting to ForgeTest also whites out Oakvale (shared-state corruption).

findings.claim: The DOMINANT, provable white-out mechanism is bank resource resolution BY MAP NAME, not by index-in-chunk. At map-open the engine looks up the current map name in a std::map<CCharString,long> (name->InfoBlock reloff) built from the file's COMMON_HEADER; a miss returns the map ROOT/sentinel node, so a custom name that is not an exact key mis-resolves the InfoBlock offset and the bank entry.
findings.engineEvidence: CEngineWorldMap::OpenMapFile @ (decomp line 974-1104): reads COMMON_HEADER, loops null-terminated map-name strings and Map_InsertStringKeyNode builds the name->reloff std::map (line 1057-1091), then calls OpenRetailStaticMap passing it as param_3 (line 1098-1101). OpenRetailStaticMap @00b41e50 (line 420): iVar5=StdMap_FindLE(this+0x1c) — looks up the map NAME at this+0x1c; line 422 seeks the stream to *(iVar5+0x14) (the resolved reloff); then CreateNewBankMap (line 430-431) and OpenStaticMap consume from there. StdMap_FindLE @ (line 1753-1783) is an exact-match std::map<CCharString> search: on no match it returns iVar1 (the header/root sentinel), NOT the intended record.
findings.discrepancy: ForgeTest.lev was cloned from donor and its bank/graphic resources exist only under the donor's name. StdMap_FindLE('ForgeTest') therefore misses the exact-key match and returns the sentinel, so the InfoBlock reloff and bank entry index are wrong for ForgeTest -> textures/mesh resolve to the wrong/empty entry => white. This is by NAME; BankFileIndex=426 in the InfoBlock is never consulted here (CreateNewBankMap takes an entry index derived from the resolved node, not the InfoBlock field).
findings.toolingEvidence: NATIVE_TERRAIN_STATUS.md:88 confirms forge stb list shows entry 426 = ...ForgeTest.lev keyed by FULL PATH identical to 398 siblings (the crash-fix), but that only fixes the mandatory-entry crash; the by-name resolve at StdMap_FindLE still keys on the runtime map name at this+0x1c. stbbake.cpp:150-346 (retargetChunk) only rewires the quadtree/mesh bytes and never touches name/theme resolution, so it is a verified no-op for the white-out.

findings.claim: CreateNewBankMap binds the bank resource by ENTRY INDEX/OFFSET, not by a FindIndexBySymbol(name) call — so the by-name steering happens upstream (StdMap_FindLE), and the bind itself trusts whatever index that name-resolve produced.
findings.engineEvidence: CEngineWorldMap::CreateNewBankMap @009d58d0 (decomp line 1796-1839): receives entry arg in_stack_00000008 and calls CBankFile::GetEntryDataSize((CBankFile*)this, in_stack_00000008) then Align — pure index-driven; there is NO FindIndexBySymbol / name compare in the body.
findings.discrepancy: Confirms the address/mechanism reconciliation in TERRAIN_RENDER_FIX.md:17: the proven call target is 009d58d0 (not the doc's earlier 009e0360/009d58d0 confusion) and the bind is by index. The name only matters through the upstream StdMap_FindLE that produces that index. An FSE name-alias at this+0x1c before StdMap_FindLE is therefore the correct minimal intercept for mechanism (A).

findings.fix: Two-part, matching the two proven mechanisms. (A) Bank-by-name (dominant, high-confidence): make ForgeTest resolve under a name that is an exact key in the region's COMMON_HEADER name->reloff std::map. Either (i) FSE map-open name-alias: hook OpenRetailStaticMap @00b41e50 and rewrite the CEngineMap name at this+0x1c from 'ForgeTest.lev' to the donor 'Darkwood9_Leadout_01' for exactly one open (this lands before StdMap_FindLE at line 420) — this is the already-built diagnostic in TERRAIN_RENDER_FIX.md §2 and will render the DONOR terrain, proving (A); or (ii, durable) run the editor bake so ForgeTest gets its OWN COMMON_HEADER name-key + bank entry baked under its own name, making StdMap_FindLE('ForgeTest') an exact hit. Note the InfoBlock BankFileIndex is a red herring — CreateNewBankMap @009d58d0 binds by the index StdMap_FindLE yields, not by that field. (B) Theme-by-index (name-agnostic co-cause, medium-confidence): if terrain still whites out after (A), the donor's per-map palette seeds a global ENGINE_THEME def-index that is out-of-range/absent in ForgeTest's region context. BuildThemes @00b687d0 already bounds-checks (line 557-566, falls back to bank ptr 0). The clamp/fix is to guarantee the theme def-index seeded into the CMap palette (AddThemeDefIndexToPalette @008f70f0, seeded in CMap_InitializePalette @008f71a0 from *(*(*(this+0x1c)+0xd0)+0x50)) corresponds to a theme that BuildThemes actually populated — i.e. bake under ForgeTest's own region so the .LEV ground-theme names (lev.cpp:96) map to resident ENGINE_THEME indices. The editor bake covers BOTH (A) and (B); the FSE alias covers only (A). Run the FSE alias first as a bisector: donor terrain renders + Oakvale stops whiting out => (A) is the cause; still white => (B) contributes and needs the bake or a BuildThemes index clamp.

findings.suspect: theme-palette-build (CMap_InitializePalette 0x008f71a0 + AddThemeDefIndexToPalette 0x008f70f0 + ZeroAllUnusedThemePaletteEntries 0x008f6fc0): the per-map theme palette is built by theme DEF-INDEX; hypothesis was that a donor chunk's palette-local indices map to the wrong/empty theme in a new map context, whiting the terrain.

findings.claim: The per-map theme palette IS index-keyed, but by GLOBAL CDefinitionManager theme-def indices (ENGINE_THEME namespace) — NOT by region-local or chunk-local ids. The same byte value resolves to the same global theme in every map on the same install, so a byte-clone of a donor chunk does not remap themes.
findings.engineEvidence: CMap_InitializePalette@0x008f71a0 (line 706-728): zeroes 0x800-byte palette at CMap+0x1a6c (256 entries x 8 bytes: [dword global-def-index][byte used-flag][pad]), then seeds ONE entry via AddThemeDefIndexToPalette(this, *(ulong*)(*(int*)(*(int*)(this+0x1c)+0xd0)+0x50)). The seed value is pulled from a runtime def-object chain (CMap+0x1c -> +0xd0 -> +0x50), not from the STB chunk. AddThemeDefIndexToPalette@0x008f70f0 (line 742-788) stores that dword verbatim into a palette slot (*(ulong*)(this+0x1a6c + slot*8)=param_1) and returns the palette-LOCAL slot (uchar 0-255). BuildThemes@0x00b687d0 (line 512-536) shows those dword indices are indices into the GLOBAL CEngineLandscapeRenderer theme vector, sized to LTextSystem::GetIDFromSymbol(DAT_01436e28,"ENGINE_THEME") and filled by GetDef<CSoundThemeDef>(DAT_01436e28,"ENGINE_THEME",idx) — a global, name-derived, install-wide table shared by every map.
findings.toolingEvidence: assemble_forgetest_terrain.py:11-14 deliberately picks donor Darkwood9_Leadout_01 for the "SAME spooky/Darkwood theme family so ground textures resolve against the same graphics.big entries", i.e. the donor and target draw from one shared global theme/graphics table. NATIVE_STB_WRITER_SCOPE.md:22-25 confirms "No theme field in CStaticMapInfoBlock (0x5C)" and "BuildThemes reads the global ENGINE_THEME table shared by every map". Grep of stb_infoblock_baker.py, stbbake.cpp, stbvalidate.cpp, assemble_forgetest_terrain.py finds ZERO theme/palette handling — the tooling never touches theme grid or palette bytes, so any grid bytes in the cloned chunk are carried over unchanged from the donor.
findings.discrepancy: The hypothesised discrepancy does NOT exist: there is no region-local or per-context theme index space that a relocated chunk could mis-key. The palette is keyed by GLOBAL def indices resolved through one install-wide CDefinitionManager table. A byte-identical donor chunk in a new map slot, on the same game install, resolves to the exact same global themes. The theme-palette-build path is therefore context-invariant w.r.t. a byte-clone relocation and cannot by itself produce the white-out.

findings.claim: Per-cell theme grid bytes ARE palette-LOCAL indices (0-255), confirming the two-level index scheme — but this only shifts the question to whether the grid+palette are self-consistent within the cloned chunk, which they are (both cloned together from the donor).
findings.engineEvidence: GetEngineThemeAt@0x0081f090 (line 3025-3031, the render/query consumer): for paint-type 0 it returns *(ulong*)(this+0x1a6c + (grid_cell_byte)*8), where grid_cell_byte is read from the theme grid at CMap+0x1a7c (base +0x10, dims at +0x204/+0x208, cell stride 0xc, byte at cell+4+param3). The grid byte is used DIRECTLY as the palette-local slot index. ZeroAllUnusedThemePaletteEntries@0x008f6fc0 (line 824-855) walks the SAME grid (this+0x1a7c, +0x10 base, 0xc stride, bytes at +4/+5/+6) and marks each referenced palette slot used — proving grid cells hold palette-local byte indices, and the palette+grid form one self-contained pair.
findings.toolingEvidence: Because the STB payload is a byte-identical clone (assemble_forgetest_terrain.py:6-7, sha256 match; only structural offset dwords 0x20/0x24/0x58/0x5C/0x71 rebased per rebase_chunk lines 121-129), the donor's theme grid bytes and their palette-seed travel together intact. The grid->palette->global-def chain stays internally consistent in the clone.
findings.discrepancy: No self-consistency break: grid bytes and the palette that interprets them are both cloned from the same donor, so the local index space matches. The only way this path breaks is if the global ENGINE_THEME table differs between donor-bake time and target-open time — i.e. a DIFFERENT game install/def-set — which is not the case here (same retail install).

findings.fix: No fix belongs in the theme-palette-build path; do not add a BuildThemes index clamp or any theme-registration writer (NATIVE_STB_WRITER_SCOPE.md:22-25 already concluded there is no theme surface to register, and this decomp trace confirms why: indices are global/install-wide, not region-local). Redirect the fix effort to the ACTUAL shared-state map-open surface: (1) the by-name bank/graphic-bank resolution in OpenRetailStaticMap@0x00b41e50 -> CreateNewBankMap (the chunk's scenery/graphic bank resources exist only under the donor name Darkwood9_Leadout_01 and fail to resolve for ForgeTest.lev), and/or (2) confirm textures render via the chunk's own inline DXT1 (NATIVE_TERRAIN_STATUS.md:16 notes the chunk is self-textured with zero name-strings). The durable route remains the editor bake which registers ForgeTest's own bank under its own name (both mechanisms at once). If a cheap bisection is wanted, the FSE name-alias (TERRAIN_RENDER_FIX.md §2) that renames this+0x1c to the donor for one map-open tests the by-name-bank hypothesis directly — and since themes are name-agnostic/global, that alias does nothing to themes, which is consistent with themes NOT being the cause.

It reads a leading count then loops building CLocalDetailObjectCollectionType entries.

It is at most a secondary scenery-population effect.

BuildThemes resizes a GLOBAL theme vector by ENGINE_THEME def-count and populates each entry by def-INDEX via CDefinitionManager::GetDef<CSoundThemeDef>(idx).

But it is a DIFFERENT function group than the assigned suspect and cannot be pinned to proof from this dump either (no per-block theme-index reader for the landscape is shown).
findings.toolingEvidence: NATIVE_TERRAIN_STATUS.md §1 line 19 and TERRAIN_RENDER_FIX.md §1 both flag BuildThemes theme-by-index (DAT_01436e28/DAT_01436e98) as name-agnostic and un-modeled by the harness; NATIVE_TERRAIN_STATUS.md §4 line 92 notes CStaticMapInfoBlock has no theme field, so themes are resolved by the global index table, not from the chunk's InfoBlock.

findings.fix: My assigned suspect (detail-cache open, 00bdf010 / 00bdedd0) is not the white-out cause and needs no fix: it loads scenery/foliage collection types (by name-symbol + ability-level against global singletons), never a ground material or theme index, and contains no NULL/default-white material branch. To actually locate the white-ground default path, decompile the function NOT in this dump: CEngineTexturePalette::Load (the ground-texture palette loaded from CEngineLandscapeMap::OpenStaticMap @ landscape+0x40, call site at decomp line 1925) — that is where the ground material id/index is read and where a default/white fallback would be taken. In parallel, treat the index-based theme path (BuildThemes @00b687d0 + CMap_InitializePalette @008f71a0 + AddThemeDefIndexToPalette @008f70f0) as the leading live co-suspect: it builds a GLOBAL theme table by ENGINE_THEME def-INDEX, so a donor chunk carrying donor-context theme/texture indices that don't resolve in the new region would take the wrong/empty entry and can corrupt shared global state (explaining Oakvale whiting out too). Concretely: (1) pull and decompile CEngineTexturePalette::Load to confirm whether the chunk references texture bank entries by index vs name and where it defaults to white; (2) dump the landscape per-block theme-index reader to prove index mismatch. The durable fix remains the editor rebake (registers ForgeTest's own texture-bank + theme indices under its own region context), since neither the detail-cache nor any chunk-byte edit can register those indices.

findings.toolingEvidence: TERRAIN_RENDER_FIX.md:18 and NATIVE_TERRAIN_STATUS.md:19 flag BuildThemes theme-by-index as the name-agnostic co-suspect; no tooling models or clamps it.
findings.discrepancy: Mechanism (b) is real but does NOT live in the InfoBlock, so it is out of scope for the infoblock-refs suspect; it cannot be fixed by editing InfoBlock fields.

findings.fix: Do NOT pursue an InfoBlock-field fix for the white-out; it is the wrong surface.
